references.text: The instructions for the ordination of priests in Exodus 29 provide the detailed basis that is now carried out in Leviticus 8.
The Lord commands Moses to anoint Aaron and his sons for priestly service, a command fulfilled in Leviticus 8.
Refers to the ordination of Aaron and his sons as priests, which was carried out according to the Lord's command to Moses.
The same formula 'the Lord spoke to Moses' is used repeatedly to introduce divine commands.
The same introductory formula where the Lord speaks to Moses, which is characteristic of Leviticus.
Hebrews explains that no one takes honor for themselves as high priest, but must be called by God, just as Aaron was called through Moses.
